verdict: Lend selectively to Itanagar horticulture and floriculture only where the borrower has a confirmed buyer, a working cold chain and a repayment schedule matched to harvest cash; the data pack gives no score, so treat this as a first-principles call, not a green light.
title: Itanagar horticulture & floriculture: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business actually is
**This is a harvest-to-cash business, not a farm-asset business.** A grower puts in planting material, labour and orchard upkeep for years, then sells a perishable crop in a short window; kiwi from Itanagar has now gone as a trial shipment to Dubai, showcased at LuLu Hypermarket in Al Qusais [1], and a first cut-flower consignment went to Guwahati with farmers earning Rs 1L [3]. **Cash sits in the dispatch window, not in the field** — so when a proposal lands, check the buyer, the dispatch month and who bears transit loss before you look at the land.

## Where value and cash sit
**Pricing power is thin and freight-heavy.** The kiwi line is described as a maiden trial shipment [1] and the flower line as a first consignment [3]; neither is a repeat contract yet. **Working capital is the real exposure:** packing, grading and cold movement are paid before the buyer pays. Capex is modest — packhouses, grading sheds, basic cold storage — and should be the only thing we fund as term debt. **Ask for the buyer's name, the per-kg realisation and the payment terms; collect from customer where the proposal is silent.**

## What has changed now
**The change is market access, not yield.** State departments, APEDA and the Kiwi Growers Cooperative Society drove the Dubai trial [1], and the government is pushing data-driven agri projects through NERAMAC [2]. **Peer results are mixed and should not be read as a sector signal:** Pushpanjali Floriculture's March 2026 net sales rose 40.95% to Rs 13.18 crore but it posted a net loss of Rs 2.15 crore with EBITDA negative at Rs 0.24 crore [6]; Nagarjuna Agri-Tech's June 2026 quarter sales were INR 321.81 million against INR 15.31 million a year ago [5], with erratic profit [7]. **Sources say little about Itanagar specifically** — the local items are single consignments, so lean on first principles and these peers.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue the aggregator, not the individual smallholder:** cooperative-linked kiwi growers with a named export buyer [1], cut-flower growers selling into Guwahati with repeat dispatches [3], and packhouse or grading units serving them. **Avoid single-season, single-buyer growers** and anyone whose only evidence is a trial shipment [1]. **Take a charge on receivables and a second charge on the orchard or shed; size the limit to one dispatch cycle, not one year.**

## What to take every month and what to watch
**Monthly: dispatch invoices, buyer payment receipts, cold-storage bills and a stock-and-mortality statement.** If receipts lag invoices by more than one cycle, stop fresh disbursement and ask for the buyer's confirmation. **If a second consignment does not follow the first [1][3], treat the line as unproven and shift to cash-backed limits.**
watch: receipts lag invoices by one cycle -> stop fresh disbursement, seek buyer confirmation
no second shipment after the trial [1][3] -> downgrade to cash-backed limit
single buyer above half of sales -> ask for a second buyer or reduce limit
losses rise on the Dubai or Guwahati route -> reprice or exit the line
